result.title: Semantic Residual Vector Quantization for Sign Language Generation
result.summary: Sign language generation (SLG) maps written sentences into signing motion while preserving both lexical content and fine-grained articulation. This requires a model to decide what signs should be expressed and to realize them through precise handshape, trajectory, facial expression and body coordination. Existing pose-based systems and reconstruction-only motion tokenizers often entangle these two decisions, leaving the generator without an explicit text-aligned intermediate target for what to sign before refining how to sign it. To address this issue, we introduce Semantic Residual Vector Quantization (SRVQ), a framework for SLG that frames generation as a two-level process moving from semantics to kinematics. The newly introduced SRV Quantizer learns a hierarchy in which the first residual level encodes sign content and subsequent levels refine pose, handshape, trajectory, and body coordination, all within a single quantizer and without separate semantic representations or external planning stages. Through word-aware conditioning for hierarchical code generation, a masked semantic generator predicts semantic codes and a kinematic generator completes the residual codes for full SMPL-X motion synthesis. We evaluate using retrieval and FID in a shared text-motion embedding space, alongside standard geometric metrics. On CSL-Daily and Phoenix-2014T, SRVQ achieves R@1 of 82.3 and 70.3, outperforming the previous SOTA by 30 and 46 points, respectively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SRVQ，将文本到手语动作生成拆为语义与运动学两级：首个 residual 量化层编码手语内容，后续层细化姿态、手形与轨迹，并用词级条件的分层码生成器完成 SMPL-X 动作合成。
AI.relevance_reason: 残差量化的分层 latent（语义层对应「说什么」、后续层对应「怎么做」）与词级对齐监督，可能为 LVR 中按内容/细节分级组织 latent 状态及层级监督提供核查线索，但任务是动作生成，与 VLM 推理相距较远。
